title: Odysseus Strings the Bow
part: The Metis mod line, proof 03: the hall's causal map (odyssey/metis/README.md; the fieldbook's note: 'Daylight and roofless views make the room resemble a displayed set. The arrow line, exit doors and storeroom access must become a stable geography before violence.')
hypothesis: The turn of the bow reads with captions off if the room is a real interior at night (roofed, lit only by the hearth and torches) and its geography is fixed before the shot: the sill-to-axes line established first, the doors seen open and then shut, the pegs seen bare, and the arrow seen going through all twelve sockets on that line, ending on the same axis now held by the archer.
variable: The world and the light: the forage's roofless daylight megaron with a prop row of axes -> the Bow and the Hall kit (staging_hall.py) with a roof, doors on hinges, bare weapon pegs, twelve axes whose sockets stand on one line at bow height and a Technic-axle arrow slid through them on the loose; firelight (odyssey-light.js, looks/hearth-hall.json). And the shots that carry the geography (seven of twelve pinned by hand: tools/metis/hall.py).

result: Kept. The room is an interior at night: roofed, lit only by its fires, the faces yellow and their printed eyes readable. The geography is laid before the shot: the line from the porch through the open doors, the doors seen open and then shut, the bare pegs beside the two men, the arrow carried through the twelve sockets on one line and out past the last, the axis held from its far end at the close. Loose: the arrow's passage is a thin rod in a high side shot (the sockets hide it from the sill); the doors swing with no hand on them; the opening wide through the doors is slow to draw; the reversal with captions off has not been tried on a viewer; the HOT and REACT shots are still the solver's.

previous.result: Kept. The film now opens on the act: Odysseus at mid size with the bow in his hands, the horn braced and the bow bending through STRING_BOW's bends under 'strings the bow effortlessly'; the shot moves on almost every drawing (still 0.45 -> 0.05). Loose: the opening shot and shot 1 are both mids of Odysseus from nearby angles, so the cut at 5.2 s is close to a jump cut; the hall is no longer established before the reaction shots (the wide at 15.5 s still does it later); the bends themselves are small (STRING_BOW's amplitudes were not this take's variable) and a grey prop in the foreground crowds the left of frame.
